newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Zastava foreign partner known by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Zastava foreign partner known by year-end.

text.p: Yugoslavia's car producer Zastava is currently talking with three potential foreign partners and will choose one of them by the year-end, Belgrade papers reported on Monday.
"I would be happy if a deal with a foreign partner could be signed tomorrow," the papers quoted Zastava group general manager Srboljub Vasovic as saying. "But two sides are needed for a deal."
"How can we force a foreign partner to sign a deal with us so that none of the workers lose their job," Vasovic said. "But the foreign partner who invests the money also dictates certain conditions."

Vasovic said many (foreign partners) described Zastava's demands as impossible. "That is not correct. We want the entire production to continue, not just assembly or spraying as foreign partners want."
Analysts estimate that about 8,000 out of 15,000 or so employees in car manufacture will have to go if the car plant is to become profitable.
"Our interest is to engage as many workers and capacities as possible and to survive as a car producer," Vasovic said.
Hit by the break-up of former Yugoslavia and 3-1/2 years of crippling U.N. sanctions, Zastava's car production has slumped to 8,000 vehicles in 1995, from as high as 200,000 in 1990.

Kragujevac, where the plant is located in the heartland of Yugoslavia's industrial belt, has seen protests over unpaid wages and lack of work in the past month by workers at Zastava's sister factory producing weapons.
